PRENATAL ARRAY CGH REPORT

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]

Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal testing

SPECIMEN TYPE
Uncultured placental material

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
QF-PCR for triploidy exclusion

METHODOLOGY
Oligonucleotide array analysis was performed using the GeneScreen 5000 design containing approximately 60,000 genome-wide probes. DNA was extracted from uncultured placental material and processed according to manufacturer's protocols. Analysis was performed using GenomeAnalyzer software with reference to the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly. The analytical sensitivity for detection of genomic imbalances is >1Mb across the genome, with enhanced coverage in clinically relevant regions allowing detection of smaller pathogenic imbalances.

Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) was performed to exclude triploidy using markers for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y.

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH RESULT:
arr(1-22)x2,(XY)x1

INTERPRETATION: Normal male chromosome complement

No genomic imbalances >1Mb were detected across chromosomes 1-22, X, and Y. No smaller pathogenic imbalances were identified in regions of known clinical significance.

QF-PCR RESULT:
Normal diallelic pattern consistent with diploid male karyotype. No evidence of triploidy.

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
This analysis reveals a normal male chromosome complement with no significant genomic imbalances detected. The resolution of this test excludes most chromosome abnormalities associated with developmental disabilities and congenital anomalies.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required based on these results.

LIMITATIONS
• This test cannot detect balanced chromosome rearrangements, low-level mosaicism (<20%), or point mutations
• Some regions of the genome have limited probe coverage due to repetitive sequences
• Uniparental disomy and methylation abnormalities are not detected by this methodology
• Results are limited to the specimen submitted and may not be representative of all fetal tissues
• Maternal cell contamination, if present, may affect results

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted laboratory name]. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is regulated under CLIA as qualified to perform high-complexity clinical testing.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
